Farhan caught me at the lift, quietly, like he was handing over a parcel. “People are saying you got the senior role because you're close to the director, and that you and Meera from finance are together.” I laughed it off, but by afternoon I could feel it: the pantry going quiet, eyes sliding away. I'm Nitin, by the way.

For two weeks I arrived at eight, wore my sharpest shirt and never left before the director did, just so nobody could say I was slacking. I stopped talking to Meera altogether. It was exhausting. I spent more energy on what they thought than on my actual work. One evening Sanjay, who never gossips, said, “You look tired, man. Are you okay?” And I nearly cried.

qa.a: Farhan caught Nitin at the lift and quietly said what people were saying about the senior role.

qa.q: Why did Nitin start arriving at eight and never leave before the director?
qa.a: Nitin felt anxious and watched after hearing the rumours, so managing the impression that nobody could call Nitin a slacker became more urgent than the actual work.

qa.q: What did Sanjay do that helped Nitin near the end?
qa.a: Sanjay, who never gossips, asked if Nitin was okay, which let Nitin drop the act and nearly cry.

qa.q: What might Meera feel after Nitin stopped talking to Meera altogether?
qa.a: Meera might feel confused, hurt and unfairly dragged into the talk.

grounding: An employee finds out that people at work speculate about their promotion and personal life, feels exposed and over-manages their image.

I can't say what he was feeling. He looked like someone on a stage. Pooja from payroll, who had started half of it, kept glancing at him and then at her screen. Wednesday night. Third week at the new college. I've started noticing how people sort each other. First it's “Which college were you at before?” Then it's who speaks English fastest, then whose phone is newest, then whose uncle knows the dean. At the canteen today Sabina said she came from a small-town college. Nobody laughed, but the table went quiet and Rhea asked, “Oh. Is that... a good place?” Sabina smiled too quickly. She answers everything twice as brightly now.

I felt strange sitting there, because I had put myself on the safe side without even thinking.

Note to self: notice who I'm not asking to sit.
— Minakshi
